findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row.
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no `topic_users` row for the topic. That happens when they get emails through category or tag watching, or when they were mentioned in a topic they never opened. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link in the email returns a 500 error. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row if needed, or handle the nil case before reading the level.

findings.title: `unsubscribe_link` now needs `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which other emails don't pass.
findings.body: MessageBuilder calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` now passes `unsubscribe_url`. Other mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link` (digest and similar) will hit `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` or render a broken string. The spec had to add `unsubscribe_url` just to keep passing, which shows the same failure. I could not see the other mailers, so check them. Fix: use a separate key for the per-topic line and add it only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: A GET request changes notification state and has no CSRF protection.
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is a plain GET that writes `notification_level` with no token. Any third-party page, image tag or email link prefetcher that loads `/t/x/123/unsubscribe` for a logged-in user silently changes their notification level for that topic. The change also steps down on every load: watching/tracking → regular, then regular → muted. So reloading the page, or a prefetch followed by a click, mutes the topic even though the user only asked to stop emails. Make the change idempotent (always set one target level). Better still, show a confirmation page and apply the change with a POST/PUT that carries a CSRF token, or require a signed per-user token in the link.
